title: Drawn from the data
description:
In immediate mode the interface is rebuilt from the data every frame, so it can never be out of date. Write the text lines a debug window would show for a list of enemies:

```cpp
struct Enemy { std::string name; int hp; };

std::vector<std::string> enemyWindow(const std::vector<Enemy>& enemies);
```

- The first line is `"Enemies alive: N"`, counting enemies with `hp > 0`.
- Then one line per **living** enemy, in order: `"<name> (<hp> hp)"`.
- If none are alive, the second line is `"(none)"`.

Call it twice with different data and you get two different "frames": nothing has to be updated or removed.
